script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 10. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

A rainbow isn't really there—not like a tree or a building.  It's an optical phenomenon, a trick of light and geometry.  Each raindrop is a tiny prism, bending sunlight and sending colors toward your eyes.

Light enters a raindrop and bends—that's refraction. It reflects off the back of the drop and exits, bending again. Each color bends at a slightly different angle: red least, violet most. That's what fans white light into a spectrum. Each raindrop creates its own complete rainbow.  But you only see one color from each drop, depending on the angle.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: White light contains all colors.  What appears simple—a beam of sunlight—holds hidden complexity.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Hidden Spectrum - Look Deeper.

Here's your activity: Choose something 'simple' in your life—a relationship, a habit, a routine task. Spend 5 minutes exploring its hidden complexity. What 'colors' are hiding in the white light of the obvious? This helps you practice seeing complexity in seemingly simple things.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how rainbows form can be applied to hidden spectrum - look deeper. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
